# HorizontalButterflyBarChart

## Overview

The HorizontalButterflyBarChart displays two series growing outward from a center axis, commonly used for:

- Population pyramids (age distribution by gender)
- Year-over-year comparisons (2023 vs 2024)
- Before/after analysis
- Any dual-series comparison with a shared dimension

## Figma Reference

- **Node ID**: `262:8111`
- **Design File**: DataVis-Components
- **Figma URL**: https://www.figma.com/design/uA5ExvS0cNXbDEKzT9Rnrt/DataVis-Components?node-id=262-8111

## Architecture

```
HorizontalButterflyBarChart (flex column, gap: var(--Spacing-5))
├── ChartHeader (optional, if chartHeader=true)
│   ├── ChartTitle
│   └── ChartSubtitle
├── ChartLegend (optional, if chartLegend=true)
│   └── ChartKey[] (auto-generated or manual items)
├── DataDisplay (optional, if dataDisplay=true)
│   ├── contentLeft
│   │   ├── mainLabel
│   │   └── DataHead (DataLead + SupportingData + SupportingLabel)
│   └── contentRight (Badge)
├── HorizontalButterflyBarGroup (flex: 1)
│   ├── contentWrapper
│   │   └── HorizontalButterflyBar[] (for each category)
│   └── XAxis (dual mirrored scales)
└── ChartFooter (optional, if chartFooter=true)
    ├── annotationLeft
    └── annotationRight
```

## Import

```tsx
import { HorizontalButterflyBarChart } from './charts/HorizontalButterflyBarChart';
```

## Data Formats

Uses canonical `ChartSeriesDataPoint[]` format with exactly 2 series per category:

```tsx
const data: ChartSeriesDataPoint[] = [
  { category: '0–14',  series: 'Male',   value: 15 },
  { category: '0–14',  series: 'Female', value: 18 },
  { category: '15–24', series: 'Male',   value: 22 },
  { category: '15–24', series: 'Female', value: 24 },
];
```

The first series (by `seriesOrder` or insertion order) becomes the left bar; the second becomes the right bar.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |

### ChartLegendConfig

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `ChartLegendItem[]` | `undefined` | Manual legend items (overrides auto-generated) |
| `leftLabel` | `string` | Auto-detected | Override left series legend label |
| `rightLabel` | `string` | Auto-detected | Override right series legend label |
| `type` | `'circle' \| 'dashed' \| 'line'` | `'circle'` | Legend swatch shape |
| `dataHead` | `boolean` | `false` | Show DataHead block in both auto-generated legend items (left + right) |
| `dataHeadConfig` | `object` | `undefined` | DataHead configuration applied to both auto-generated legend items (see sub-table below) |
| `size` | `'XS' \| 'S' \| 'M' \| 'L' \| 'XL'` | `undefined` | Typography size variant controlling legend item scaling |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `"Chart legend"` | Forwarded to ChartLegend's `aria-label` |
| `ariaLabelledBy` | `string` | `undefined` | Forwarded to ChartLegend's `aria-labelledby`; takes precedence over `ariaLabel` when set |

> **Note**: `categoryLabelValue` (a single-series legend label, documented on `HorizontalBarChart`) does not apply here — butterfly charts are always 2-series, so use `leftLabel`/`rightLabel` instead.

| `supportingLabelValue` | `string` | `undefined` | Supporting label text for DataHead |

## Usage Examples

### Minimal

```tsx
import { HorizontalButterflyBarChart } from './charts/HorizontalButterflyBarChart';

<HorizontalButterflyBarChart
  data={populationData}
  width={500}
  height={550}
  barGroupConfig={{ seriesOrder: ['Male', 'Female'] }}
/>
```

### With header and legend

```tsx
<HorizontalButterflyBarChart
  data={populationData}
  width={500}
  height={550}
  chartHeader
  chartLegend
  chartHeaderConfig={{
    chartTitleValue: 'Population Distribution',
    chartSubtitleValue: 'By age group and gender',
  }}
  barGroupConfig={{
    seriesOrder: ['Male', 'Female'],
    labelOutside: true,
  }}
/>
```

### Auto height (content-driven)

```tsx
<HorizontalButterflyBarChart
  data={sparseData}
  width={500}
  chartHeader
  chartLegend
  chartHeaderConfig={{ chartTitleValue: 'Product Comparison' }}
  barGroupConfig={{
    seriesOrder: ['2023', '2024'],
    autoHeight: true,
    labelOutside: true,
  }}
/>
```

When the dataset has only one or a few rows, the default fixed-height layout leaves rows at the top of the butterfly-bar area and the dual X-axis pinned to the bottom of the chart, with a large void in between. Set `barGroupConfig.autoHeight: true` to collapse the chart container to fit its content instead:

- The chart container's `height` prop is **ignored** — the container collapses to `header + legend + dataDisplay + bars + X-axis + footer` at their natural sizes
- The chart's `barGroupWrapper` switches from `flex: 1` to `flex: 0 0 auto` so the group doesn't stretch
- `HorizontalButterflyBarGroup.autoHeight: true` is forwarded so the group switches its `contentWrapper` to `flex: 0 0 auto` with a token-driven gap between rows — the dual X-axis sits immediately below the last row

Unlike `HorizontalBarChart`/`HorizontalDumbbellChart` (where `autoHeight` is a top-level chart prop), this chart nests it under `barGroupConfig.autoHeight` — check the top of this doc's Props table for the current location before wiring it up.

### Minimal — bars only

```tsx
<HorizontalButterflyBarChart
  data={populationData}
  width={480}
  height={500}
  chartHeader={false}
  chartLegend={false}
  dataDisplay={false}
  chartFooter={false}
  barGroupConfig={{
    seriesOrder: ['Male', 'Female'],
    labelOutside: true,
  }}
/>
```

## Legend Auto-detection

When `chartLegendConfig.items` is not supplied, the chart auto-detects two series names from `data` (or uses `seriesOrder` when provided) and creates legend items using the DataVis categorical colour tokens:

```
Series 0 → var(--DataVis-Categorical-Bold-1)
Series 1 → var(--DataVis-Categorical-Bold-2)
```

Use `chartLegendConfig.leftLabel` / `rightLabel` to show a display-friendly label in the legend without changing `seriesOrder`.

Set `chartLegendConfig.dataHead: true` (optionally with `dataHeadConfig`) to show a DataHead value block in both auto-generated legend items, and `chartLegendConfig.size` to control the legend's typography scale — both are applied identically to the left and right legend item, since a butterfly chart's legend always describes exactly two series:

```tsx
<HorizontalButterflyBarChart
  data={populationData}
  chartLegend
  chartLegendConfig={{
    dataHead: true,
    dataHeadConfig: { dataLeadValue: '42%' },
    size: 'L',
  }}
/>
```

## Design Tokens

| CSS Custom Property | Resolves To | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--HorizontalButterflyBarChart-containerGap` | `var(--Spacing-5)` | Gap between chart slots (overridable) |
| `--DataVis-Categorical-Bold-1` | Brand categorical token | Left series bar and legend colour |
| `--DataVis-Categorical-Bold-2` | Brand categorical token | Right series bar and legend colour |

## Accessibility

The component is wrapped by the shared `ChartAccessibility` component (`src/components/ChartAccessibility.tsx`), enabled by default. It renders `role="figure"` with `aria-label`/`aria-describedby`, a visually hidden data table for screen readers, and an auto-generated accessible summary (worded for `chartType="butterfly-bar"`). The `accessibility` prop passes through to `AccessibilityConfig`:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable/disable all accessibility features. When `false`, the chart renders its content directly with no wrapper, hidden table, or live region |
| `summary` | `string` | Auto-generated | Custom summary text (overrides auto-generation) |
| `dataTable` | `boolean` | `true` | Render the visually-hidden data table for screen readers |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | Auto-generated | Override the chart's `aria-label` |

An ARIA live region announces the hovered bar value when `interactive=true`.
